title: Stage 4 — The Database
goal: Replace in-memory storage with a real database so data survives restarts.
summary: Tables, SQL, persistence — then swap your API's array for queries. The full stack connects.

pages.title: Why data must outlive the process
The full stack, end to end

checkpoint.prompt: SQL to read every column from table `workouts`.
checkpoint.explanation: `SELECT * FROM workouts` returns all columns and rows.

choices.text: A unique identifier for each row
The first column you add alphabetically

checkpoint.explanation: Primary keys let you reference one specific record reliably.

checkpoint.prompt: Why use `?` placeholders instead of string concatenation in SQL?

choices.text: Prevents SQL injection from malicious input
Makes queries run slower on purpose

checkpoint.explanation: Never build SQL with template strings from user input.

checkpoint.prompt: After swapping to SQLite, you restart the API. Data is still there. What changed?

choices.text: Data is stored on disk, not only in RAM
Express caches everything in the browser

checkpoint.explanation: The database file persists across process restarts.

checkpoint.prompt: User clicks Add → data survives refresh and server restart. How many layers worked together?

choices.text: Zero: the browser stores everything locally

checkpoint.explanation: You built outside-in: UI, then API, then persistence. Now they all connect.

checklist.label: SQLite table created for main entity
GET/POST use SQL instead of in-memory array
Frontend still lists and creates through API

questions.prompt: POST /workouts maps to which SQL operation?
questions.explanation: Create → INSERT. Read → SELECT. Update → UPDATE. Delete → DELETE.

choices.text: Single file, zero setup, real SQL
It replaces the need for an API

questions.explanation: SQLite is a real relational DB in a file — perfect for learning.
Outside-in: each layer attaches to the one before it.

questions.prompt: What does `NOT NULL` on a column mean?

choices.text: Every row must have a value for that column
The column is hidden from SELECT

questions.explanation: The database rejects rows missing required fields.

questions.prompt: GET /workouts/999 returns 404. The database had no row with id 999. Which layer returned 404?

choices.text: The API, after the query found nothing

questions.explanation: The DB returns no row; the API translates that into an HTTP status.
